caption: Matric jacket deposit, extra lessons, uniforms. How much did your matric year actually cost?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R18 600
p/m salary
Living in Beaufort West
slides.body:
Female, 42
Single mother, one son (16)
Job: Post office clerk
Net salary: R18 600 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: The landlord hasn't raised it in two years. I'm scared to mention it.

slides.title: Matric year costs
slides.includes: Uniform, transport, extra maths, matric jacket deposit
slides.body: He's in Grade 11. The jacket deposit alone was R1 100. I didn't see that coming.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite, the butcher, a lot of bread
slides.body: A teenage boy eats everything. I buy in bulk and it's gone by Wednesday.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: My mother's medication and prepaid electricity
slides.body: She's in Prince Albert on a pension that stops short every month.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.includes: Friday pizza, KFC after his rugby
slides.body: It's our one outing of the week. I'm not cutting it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Prepaid electricity, funeral policy for two, cellphone, stokvel, school fund, Netflix, petrol
slides.body: The stokvel is my only savings. R500 in, one payout a year, and I always spend it before it lands.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R18 600. About R18 a day. We're fine until something breaks.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon and found the school costs I'd lost track of across three months.

It's all in one place now.

No bank login needed.
